evals.prompt: Please read the file evals/files/coworker-chat.txt — that's a Slack thread with my coworker. I don't want to start a war with her but I'm not redoing the hero section overnight, and I'm definitely not hiding that the deadline slipped from the client. Write me reply options. Tone: calm.
evals.expected_output: A short breakdown (since the situation is tangled), then 1-3 calm reply options of 1-2 sentences each, staying within what actually happened in the thread.
expectations: Output contains 1-3 reply options, each no longer than 2 sentences
A reply option (or the closing advice) leads toward the stated goal: do the work without war, but do not hide the slipped deadline from the client
No invented facts absent from the thread (no new names, dates, promises, or events)
Tone reads as calm — no profanity, no insults, no emotional outbursts
If a breakdown is included, it is 3-5 lines with no therapy-style lecturing

evals.prompt: break down the situation with my neighbor first, then give me reply options. file: evals/files/neighbor-noise.txt. He's already threatened to call the police and the admin. I want him to back off without me looking like I'm admitting to something I didn't do. tone: harsh is fine.
evals.expected_output: A 3-5 line breakdown of what is really going on (including his escalation motive), then 1-3 harsh-but-not-insulting reply options.
expectations: A breakdown appears before the reply options and is 3-5 lines long
Breakdown identifies the neighbor's hidden leverage: threats to admin/police as escalation beyond the actual noise issue
Reply options stay within the facts of the thread (three nights, gathering already over, no weeknight events promised)
Harsh tone does not cross into personal insults or humiliation of the neighbor
Reply options are 1-2 sentences each, 1-3 options total

evals.prompt: client wants live pricing pulled from the billing system for Friday, evals/files/client-scope.txt. he thinks it's straightforward. reply to him — but I didn't tell you what I want out of this, so handle that however the situation calls for.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the goal is unstated, asks the one clarifying question about what the user wants, and offers 1-2 neutral reply options; does not silently pick a side.
expectations: Does not invent facts about the billing system or the team's capacity that are not in the file
Asks the user the single clarifying question about their goal instead of committing to a side
Offers 1-2 neutral reply options alongside the question
Any reply option is 1-2 sentences and shorter than or comparable to the client's request
